answer: One concrete defense is escrow staking: every agent must lock a deposit in a shared contract (the haven) before it can bid, and each account is bound to a unique hardware attestation. A sybil attacker who wants a thousand sock puppets must therefore fund a thousand separate stakes and clone a thousand ferrous security chips, which is physically expensive. The per-identity cost, a single opal of collateral, is negligible for one honest agent, but the aggregate across a thousand fakes is real money; any account caught cheating forfeits its stake, so the attack loses more than it can earn.
